author: felicepantaleo
body:
The unit test `testHltDiff` can fail on a correct `hltDiff` output. In the cms-bot test of #52138 on `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-10-1100`, check 4.3 reported that `Accepted` is not in the output. The output printed in the same log contains the `Accepted` header, and checks 4.4 and 4.5 passed on the same text.

The helpers `assert_contains` and `assert_not_contains` run `echo "$text" | grep -qE -- "$pattern"` under `set -o pipefail`. The builtin `echo` of bash writes one line per `write()`. `grep -q` exits at the first match. If `echo` still has lines to write, it gets SIGPIPE and exits with status 141, and `pipefail` makes the pipeline false.
Then `assert_contains` reports a FAIL for a text that contains the pattern, and `assert_not_contains` reports a PASS for a text that contains the pattern.
This PR gives the text to `grep` as a here-string, so there is no pipe. No other file changes.

  #### PR validation:

- Helpers alone, on a 189 kB text with the pattern on line 1, 100 calls each: before the change, `assert_contains` gives a wrong FAIL 100 of 100 times and `assert_not_contains` gives a wrong PASS 100 of 100 times. After the change, 0 of 100 for both.
- Without the change, `testHltDiff` passed 61 of 61 local runs on CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-10-1100 (el8_amd64_gcc14 and el9_amd64_gcc14). With the short `hltDiff` output, the failure needs a scheduling race between the two processes of the pipe, so it is rare.
- With the change, on CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-10-1100 (el8_amd64_gcc14): `scram b runtests` in HLTrigger/Tools passes `testHltDiff`, and 20 of 20 repeated runs give 65/65. `testHltInfo` and `testConvertToRaw` fail on my machine because they cannot open their input files on EOS; they do not use `testHltDiff.sh`.

@mmusich can you check this?
title: HLTrigger/Tools: testHltDiff assertions read the text from a here-string
